phases.label: Phase A
phases.title: Today's district
phases.summary: Heat pumps with heating and hot-water tanks; every unit of electricity comes from the grid. Observed weather, hour by hour over a year.

phases.label: Phase B
phases.title: Solar, battery, building mass
phases.summary: A ladder of scenarios on the same year: assumed rooftop solar with an export price (S1), a home battery (S2), and a thermal model of each building with a comfort band (S3). EV charging and a local energy community were tested in the optimiser only.

phases.label: Phase C
phases.title: Warmer climate and cooling
phases.summary: The S3 district in warmed and heat-wave weather from the Swiss climate scenarios, with cooling in some buildings: a central reversible heat pump or room units.

components.label: Weather
components.description: Observed outdoor temperature at Zurich/Kloten; it sets how efficiently the heat pumps run.

components.label: Controller
components.description: Decides when the heating and hot-water tanks charge and discharge. Rule-based controllers and learning controllers were compared.

components.label: Electricity tariff
components.description: Two-tier EKZ standard tariff (excl. VAT); it prices grid electricity and is what the tariff-timed rules react to.

components.label: Grid carbon intensity
components.description: Modeled hourly carbon intensity of Swiss grid electricity. Only how clean an hour is relative to the year is shown; it scores results and does not steer control.

components.label: Electricity grid
components.description: Supplies all electricity the buildings use; nothing is generated or stored on site.

components.label: Building connection
components.description: Where each building's grid electricity is metered. District results add up the six connections; the buildings share no grid connection.

components.label: Heat pump (space heating)
components.description: Turns electricity into heat; its efficiency (COP) falls as it gets colder outside.

components.label: Heat pump (hot water)
components.description: Second heat-pump device for hot water and the other warm-weather base load.

components.label: Household electricity
components.description: Appliances, lighting and everything else that is not the heat pump. Metered for the houses; built from sampled apartment meters for the apartment buildings.

components.label: Heating tank
components.description: Assumed buffer tank; the controller charges and discharges it.

components.label: Hot-water tank
components.description: Assumed tank, only where the heat pump serves a hot-water load.

components.label: Space-heating demand
components.description: Heat demand derived from measured heat-pump electricity. It is always met; indoor temperature is not modeled.

components.label: Hot-water demand
components.description: Derived warm-weather baseline of heat-pump heat (hot water and other use).

components.label: District outcomes
components.description: Totals over the six buildings: electricity bought, the highest hour, the bill and relative emissions.

components.label: Weather
components.description: Observed temperature and sunshine: sunshine drives the solar panels, and in S3 temperature and sun drive each building's heat balance.

components.label: Controller
components.description: Also runs the battery and, in S3, decides how much heat goes into the rooms within the comfort band. Compared: thermostat, solar rule, receding-horizon planner (MPC), exact optimum with perfect foresight and learning controllers.

components.label: Electricity tariff
components.description: The standard tariff plus an assumed price paid for exported solar; other tariff structures were tested as what-ifs.

components.label: Grid carbon intensity
components.description: Modeled hourly carbon intensity of Swiss grid electricity. Only how clean an hour is relative to the year is shown; it scores results and does not steer control.

components.label: Electricity grid
components.description: Supplies what solar and the battery do not cover and takes exported solar surplus at the assumed export price.

components.label: Rooftop solar
components.description: Assumed panels on every building (south, tilted), sized so a year's output roughly matches the building's electricity use and capped by the roof area. No real panels of these buildings are modeled.

components.label: Home battery
components.description: Assumed battery per building, sized by the kWh per kW of its solar panels, with a fixed round-trip efficiency.

components.label: Building connection
components.description: Balances solar, battery, grid and loads every hour; surplus solar is exported. Buildings share nothing here except in the energy-community scenario.

components.label: Local energy community
components.description: Labelled scenario solved in the optimiser only: the six buildings share surplus solar at a discounted grid fee. They are a composite, not real neighbours.
components.present_in: the six buildings as one community (scenario)

components.label: Heat pump (space heating)
components.description: Turns electricity into heat; in S3 the controller decides how much heat goes into the rooms.

components.label: Heat pump (hot water)
components.description: Second heat-pump device for hot water and the other warm-weather base load.

components.label: Household electricity
components.description: Appliances, lighting and everything else that is not the heat pump. Metered for the houses; built from sampled apartment meters for the apartment buildings.

components.label: EV charging
components.description: Labelled scenario solved in the optimiser only: two houses charge an electric car, with charging movable within an evening-to-morning window.

components.label: Heating tank
components.description: Assumed buffer tank; the controller charges and discharges it.

components.label: Hot-water tank
components.description: Assumed tank, only where the heat pump serves a hot-water load.

components.label: Space heating
components.description: S1 and S2 keep the derived demand. S3 replaces it with a thermal model of each building, so indoor temperature moves within a comfort band and the building itself stores heat.

components.label: Hot-water demand
components.description: Derived warm-weather baseline of heat-pump heat (hot water and other use).

components.label: District outcomes
components.description: Also export revenue, how much solar is used on site, and comfort in S3.

components.label: Weather
components.description: Observed or warmed weather built from the Swiss climate scenarios, with or without an inserted heat wave. Drives heat pumps, solar output and each building's heat balance.

components.label: Controller
components.description: Also decides heating and cooling within the comfort band. Compared in every climate and cooling case: thermostat, solar rule, planner (MPC) and exact optimum.

components.label: Electricity tariff
components.description: The standard tariff and the assumed export price, as in S3.

components.label: Grid carbon intensity
components.description: Modeled hourly carbon intensity of Swiss grid electricity. Only how clean an hour is relative to the year is shown; it scores results and does not steer control.

components.label: Electricity grid
components.description: Supplies what solar and the battery do not cover and takes exported solar surplus.

components.label: Rooftop solar
components.description: The Phase B panels, with output recomputed from each climate scenario's sunshine.

components.label: Home battery
components.description: Assumed battery per building, sized by the kWh per kW of its solar panels, with a fixed round-trip efficiency.

components.label: Building connection
components.description: Balances solar, battery, grid and loads every hour; surplus solar is exported.

components.label: Heat pump (heating and cooling)
components.description: Heats in winter. In cooled buildings the same reversible heat pump cools in summer (central system); the room-unit variant cools part of the floor area with separate units.

components.label: Heat pump (hot water)
components.description: Second heat-pump device for hot water and the other warm-weather base load.

components.label: Household electricity
components.description: Appliances, lighting and everything else that is not the heat pump. Metered for the houses; built from sampled apartment meters for the apartment buildings.

components.label: Heating tank
components.description: Assumed buffer tank; the controller charges and discharges it.

components.label: Hot-water tank
components.description: Assumed tank, only where the heat pump serves a hot-water load.

components.label: Rooms and building mass
components.description: The S3 thermal model of each building: heated, and cooled where cooling is installed, within a comfort band. Uncooled buildings warm up in summer.

components.label: Hot-water demand
components.description: Derived warm-weather baseline of heat-pump heat (hot water and other use).

components.label: District outcomes
components.description: Also cooling electricity, the share of it covered by solar, and hours above the comfort limit in uncooled buildings.
